title: Rome Refuses to Die
hook: Part 4. If Rome cannot defeat Hannibal directly, what does it destroy instead?
full_narration: Part 4. If Rome cannot defeat Hannibal directly, what does it destroy instead? It stops chasing his army, and starts choking his friends. [[pause:0.4]] First comes Syracuse, where Greek walls face Roman siege towers. From 214 to 212 BCE, the harbor city tightens under siege. [[voice:tense]] Then Rome turns north to Capua, Hannibal’s most important Italian ally. Roman forces ring Capua, cutting roads, fields, and hope. [[pause:0.6]] In 211 BCE, Hannibal marches near Rome to pull them away. Rome does not surrender, and Capua’s siege lines do not break. Far away in Spain, the elder Scipio brothers die fighting Carthage. [[voice:low]] In 210 BCE, young Scipio, later Africanus, receives extraordinary command in Spain. He strikes New Carthage in 209 BCE, the Barcid treasure gate. The fortress falls; Hasdrubal’s road to Hannibal begins narrowing. [[pause:0.8]] Follow for part 5.
